why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks, and the criterion fails. Step 1 of the builder brief gives the exact inputs and expected outputs that Check 1 uses: "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'". Check 1 runs those same calls and passes only when it gets "00042" and "  ab". Step 2 also tells the builder to test exactly those cases. That is a shared probe (a set of inputs with expected outputs), which the criterion forbids. The builder brief also repeats Check 3's FAIL condition almost word for word: "adding only padLeft will not meet the README line" against "a PR that adds only a padLeft section fails this check." Telling the builder to run `npm test` and write its own tests is allowed. The copied examples and the restated FAIL condition are not.
